newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures fall after initial rally on CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures fall after initial rally on CPI.

text.p: U.S. debt futures fell early on profit-taking which emerged after the market rallied on U.S. May consumer price data, traders said.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent and gained 0.2 percent excluding food and energy prices, versus average trade estimates for 0.2-percent increases in both rates.
"There was a lot of good news already priced into the market," John Nyhoff, chief economist and vice president at Tokyo-Mitsubishi Futures (USA) Inc, said.
Before the numbers were released, September T-bonds inched up to the overnight high of 112-06/32.
After the number was released, September popped up to 112-10/32, through Monday's high of 112-07/32.
U.S. May housing starts and the weekly BTM/Schroders U.S. chain store sales number also confirmed that the U.S. economic growth rate was not sparking a higher rate of inflation, they said.

Housing starts fell for the third month in a row, with May's seasonally-adjusted annual rate at 1.397 million units, compared to average trade estimates of 1.47 million units and against April's downwardly revised rate of 1.468 million units.

BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales index for the week ended June 14 was unchanged, as expected, from the previous week. Its month-to-date index slipped 0.3 percent from the prior month, while sales for the week were up 3.2 percent on a year-over-year basis.
Sellers immediately emerged once September T-bonds hit 112-10/32, and one market source said about 7,000 contracts were sold through the 111-31/32 level.
Floor traders said the decline was part of the classic "buy-the-rumor, sell-the-fact" trade. They dismissed comments by Cathy Minehan, president of Boston's Federal Reserve Bank.
Minehan said the Federal Reserve should continue to be vigilant in its fight against inflation.
However, the Federal Reserve's May industrial production and capacity utilization numbers did inspire fresh selling pressures, pushing September to support at 111-20/32.
The contract broke below Monday's low of 111-23/32 on the data, which aroused ideas that the market may have peaked in the short-term. Meanwhile, December Eurodollars held above support at 93.82.
Production rose 0.4 percent and use was up to 83.7 percent, versus estimates for up 0.2 percent and 83.4 percent.
Support for September T-bonds is at 111-16/32 and at 111-11/32, which currently corresponds to a cash long bond yield of 6.75 percent.

At 0844 CDT/1344 GMT, September T-bonds were off 12/32 at 111-22/32, 10-year notes fell 07/32 at 108-11/32, T-bills were down 0.005 at 94.80, and December Eurodollars were off 0.04 at 93.93. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
